description: Provenance manifest for T9: licensed external CSV reference-corpus cases adopted from independently maintained implementations. This file documents where each case in ../reference_corpora.rs came from; it is not parsed by the test itself, which embeds the actual input and expected bytes as Rust literals so byte-exact data (including invalid UTF-8) never has to round-trip through JSON.

go-encoding-csv.note: Go's readTests table annotates its Input string with position-marker glyphs (§ marks a field start, ¶ a record boundary, ∑ an error offset) that TestRead strips before parsing and uses only to check reported line/column positions coseva does not expose in the same form; those glyphs are not CSV data and are removed for every go-encoding-csv case below, noted once here rather than per case.

rust-csv.note: rust-csv is dual-licensed Unlicense/MIT; the Unlicense text is vendored here since either license permits this reuse.

excluded_sources.name: csv-spectrum
excluded_sources.reason: explicitly invites reuse but the repository carries no license file, so its cases are not vendored or adapted pending license clarification upstream

excluded_sources.name: cpython test_csv.py
excluded_sources.reason: PSF-2.0, marked optional by the T9 backlog item; omitted to keep this corpus to two independently maintained sources rather than duplicating coverage the Go and rust-csv cases already provide

excluded_sources.name: w3c-csvw
excluded_sources.reason: transformation-focused (CSV-to-JSON/RDF metadata) rather than parser-conformance-focused, and marked optional by the T9 backlog item; omitted as out of scope for a parser/emitter reference corpus

format_profiles.csv-comment-eq-delimiter: FormatOptions::CSV.comment(Some(b',')) -- rejected at construction (comment collides with the delimiter)

static_profiles.None: no built-in StaticFormat matches this profile exactly; only the dynamic FormatOptions/ParseOptions path is exercised

cases.semantic_difference: coseva has no leading-only trim policy; Whitespace trims both ends. Reused because this specific input cannot distinguish the two policies, not because they are equivalent

cases.provenance: verbatim bytes copied from the readTests table entry's Input field
cases.adaptation: Go's UseFieldsPerRecord+FieldsPerRecord=0 ("match the first record") is FieldCount::MatchFirst. Go treats the mismatch as non-fatal and keeps yielding records; coseva poisons the parser stream after any record-level error (ErrorKind::ParserFailed on the next next_line() call), so only the first mismatch is observable here
cases.expected: first record: rows [["a","b","c"]]; second record: reject FieldCountMismatch{expected:3,actual:2}
cases.semantic_difference: coseva does not resume after a field-count mismatch the way Go's reader does; a further next_line() call returns ParserFailed rather than a subsequent record

cases.provenance: verbatim bytes copied from the readTests table entry's Input field
cases.adaptation: Go's reader normalizes an embedded CRLF inside a quoted field to a bare LF ("Hello\nHi"); coseva does not perform this normalization and returns the CRLF unchanged
cases.semantic_difference: coseva preserves \r\n verbatim inside quoted fields; Go's reader collapses it to \n. This case asserts coseva's actual (different) output rather than Go's

cases.provenance: verbatim bytes copied from the readTests table entry's Input field
cases.adaptation: Go treats a bare trailing CR at end-of-input as an implicit record terminator and strips it (expected ["field1","field2"]); coseva's RecordEnding::Newline only strips a CR that is immediately followed by LF, so a trailing CR with no following LF is retained as literal field data
cases.semantic_difference: coseva keeps the trailing CR as data; Go drops it. This case asserts coseva's actual (different) output

cases.provenance: verbatim bytes copied from the readTests table entry's Input field
cases.adaptation: Go accepts a bare trailing CR right after a closing quote at end-of-input, stripping it (expected ["field"]); coseva treats any non-structural byte immediately after a closing quote as UnexpectedByteAfterQuote, including a lone CR not part of a CRLF terminator
cases.semantic_difference: coseva rejects input Go accepts. This case asserts coseva's actual (different) behavior: a rejection rather than a successful parse

cases.provenance: verbatim bytes copied from the readTests table entry's Input field
cases.adaptation: both Go (ErrQuote) and coseva (UnexpectedByteAfterQuote) reject this input, though for differently named reasons, so this case is a genuine cross-implementation agreement rather than an equivalence assumption

cases.provenance: derived from the readTests table entry's Comma/Errors fields, which drive Reader construction rather than parsing
cases.adaptation: Go's reader validates Comma/Comment lazily, on the first Read() call, and rejects a Comma of '\n' as errInvalidDelim; coseva performs the analogous validation eagerly when the parser is constructed, with ErrorKind::Configuration

cases.provenance: derived from the readTests table entry's Comma/Comment/Errors fields, which drive Reader construction rather than parsing
cases.adaptation: Go rejects a reader whose Comma and Comment runes collide (both 'X' in the upstream table) as errInvalidDelim, checked lazily on first Read(); coseva rejects the analogous FormatOptions (comment byte equal to the delimiter byte) eagerly at parser-construction time with ErrorKind::Configuration

cases.provenance: verbatim bytes copied from the `data` local of src/reader.rs's read_record_unequal_fails unit test

cases.provenance: empty input, matching the src/reader.rs headers_on_empty_data unit test

cases.semantic_difference: coseva's headers() returns Ok(None) on empty input; rust-csv's byte_headers() returns an empty-but-present record. This case asserts coseva's actual (different) behavior

cases.provenance: verbatim bytes copied from the `data` local of src/reader.rs's read_record_headers_invalid_utf8 unit test
cases.adaptation: rewritten around coseva's byte-first header API: coseva's headers() always returns byte-level headers successfully (there is no eager string-header conversion to fail the way rust-csv's headers() does); the same UTF-8 failure rust-csv reports from headers() is instead observed here by explicitly converting the byte header record with TextRecord::try_from
cases.expected: headers (bytes): ["foo","b\xFFar","baz"]; rows: [["a","b","c"],["d","e","f"]]; TextRecord::try_from(&headers) fails with InvalidUtf8
